content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In Christian teaching, 'branches' most commonly symbolize believers (disciples) in living union with Christ, who is the vine; the branches derive spiritual life from him and are expected to bear fruit, while fruitless branches face removal and judgment.","primary_basis":["John 15:1-8 (Jesus: 'I am the vine, you are the branches')","John 15:16 (appointed to bear fruit)","Psalm 80:8-16 (Israel as a vine, background imagery)","Isaiah 5:1-7 (the vineyard of the LORD, background imagery)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Covenant membership in the people of God: in Paul's olive-tree metaphor, natural branches represent Israel/Jews and grafted wild branches represent Gentile believers; broken-off branches represent unbelieving Israel, with warnings and hope of regrafting.","basis":["Romans 11:16-24","Jeremiah 11:16-17 (Israel as an olive tree whose branches are broken)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"'The Branch' (singular, Hebrew tsemach/netser) as a messianic title: a prophesied descendant of David identified in Christian interpretation with Jesus. This is a distinct but closely related usage often discussed alongside 'branches.'","basis":["Isaiah 11:1 ('a shoot from the stump of Jesse, a branch from his roots')","Jeremiah 23:5; 33:15 ('a righteous Branch' for David)","Zechariah 3:8; 6:12 ('my servant the Branch')","Isaiah 4:2","Matthew 2:23 (often linked to netser/Nazarene)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Palm branches as symbols of victory, celebration, and messianic acclamation, used at the triumphal entry and in heavenly worship.","basis":["John 12:13 (Palm Sunday)","Revelation 7:9","Leviticus 23:40 (Feast of Booths)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Branches of a great tree as nations or peoples sheltering under a kingdom's power, or the expansive growth of the kingdom of God/heaven; birds nesting in branches variously read as the nations blessed by the kingdom or (in some minority readings) as intrusive evil elements.","basis":["Ezekiel 17:22-24; 31:3-14","Daniel 4:10-22","Matthew 13:31-32; Mark 4:30-32; Luke 13:18-19"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Branches of proud trees as the arrogant or exalted who are cut down in divine judgment, or the wicked destroyed 'root and branch.'","basis":["Isaiah 10:33-34; 18:5","Malachi 4:1"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Family descendants or offspring (genealogical 'branches' of a family tree), an extension of the shoot/root imagery.","basis":["Job 15:32; 18:16","Isaiah 14:19 (contextual imagery)"],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"Consensus is strong that the plural 'branches' primarily evokes John 15: believers abiding in Christ and bearing fruit, with the Romans 11 olive-tree usage as the major secondary corporate/ecclesial reading. Interpretive debate within the John 15 reading concerns the fate of fruitless branches (loss of salvation vs. false professors vs. loss of reward), but that debate does not disturb the basic symbolic identification of branches as people connected to Christ. The singular 'Branch' as a messianic title is a distinct, well-established usage that some authors merge with the plural term. Assessment made without access to the author's material."}
